title: Program Age in the Restoration Batch Basis of a Paystride Payroll Card Program
content:
For a Paystride Payroll Card Program, the restoration batch basis — the batch figure the restoration reserve is taken on when a restoring payment is worked out — follows how long the program has been live, in whole months from its launch date to today, the whole months between two dates being the difference in calendar months less one when the later date's day of the month is smaller than the earlier date's:

1. **Fewer than 6 whole months** since launch: the restoration batch basis is the largest regular payroll batch posted since launch.
2. **At least 6 but fewer than 12 whole months** since launch: it is the greater of the most recent regular payroll batch, the one with the latest pay date, and the average regular batch.
3. **12 whole months or more** since launch, or **no launch date** on the program: the program's age does not change the restoration batch basis.

The average regular batch is the amounts of the regular payroll batches posted in the restoration look-back summed and divided by their number, or zero when none posted; the restoration look-back holds the funding entries dated today or earlier that lie fewer than three whole months before today.

### Age boundaries (hypothetical, today being 10 September)

| Launch date | Whole months since launch | Band |
|---|---|---|
| 11 March | 5 | fewer than 6 |
| 10 March | 6 | at least 6, fewer than 12 |
| 11 September of the previous year | 11 | at least 6, fewer than 12 |
| 10 September of the previous year | 12 | 12 or more |

### Hypothetical figures

- A program in its fourth month has posted regular batches of 8,120.00, 9,475.30 and 8,890.15 since launch: its restoration batch basis is the largest, 9,475.30.
- A program in its eighth month whose most recent regular batch (latest pay date) is 12,640.80 and whose average regular batch is 11,915.42 takes the greater, 12,640.80; had the most recent batch been 11,002.00, it would take the average, 11,915.42.
